title: The Subscription Stream: Notifications, Progress, and Cancellation

questions.question: A server tool list just changed. Why can it not report that change as the reply to an ordinary request?
options: The tool capability has to be renegotiated with a fresh discovery call first
The client must poll the tool list again before any change becomes visible
A reply closes the request it answers, leaving nothing open for the change
JSON-RPC does not allow a server to send an unsolicited message at all
questions.explanation: A JSON-RPC reply is tied to the one request it closes, so an ongoing change with no request in flight needs a notification on a stream instead.

questions.question: A client opens a subscriptions/listen stream with a fresh request id. What must the very first message on that stream be?
options: resources/subscribe, confirming the resource watch was registered successfully
an empty tools/list result that only confirms the new stream opened
notifications/resources/updated, reporting whatever the server produces first
notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, carrying the listen request id as subscriptionId
questions.explanation: The server must send the acknowledgment first, and it carries the id of that listen request as the subscription id in _meta, before any other notification on that stream.

questions.question: A tools/call request includes a progressToken and the server reports progress while it runs. Where do those progress notifications appear?
options: Only on the same request response channel, never on a listen stream
On a separate logging channel that is gated by a logLevel setting
On whichever stream last acknowledged a subscription for that client
On the subscriptions/listen stream, tagged with that same subscription id
questions.explanation: Progress notifications are scoped to the request that carried the progressToken and travel only on that response channel; they never carry a subscription id and never appear on a listen stream.

questions.question: A client on stdio decides to cancel a tools/call request that is still running. What should it do?
options: Close the subprocess stdin so the server treats the closed pipe as a cancel
Send a notifications/cancelled notification that names the exact request id
Send a fresh tools/call for the same id with an empty arguments object
Wait, since stdio has no way to cancel a request once it starts
questions.explanation: On stdio there is no per-request stream to close, so the client cancels by sending notifications/cancelled with the id of the request it no longer wants answered.

questions.question: A server ends a subscription during a planned shutdown, rather than the connection simply dropping. What should it send before closing the stream?
options: A fresh subscriptions/listen request of its own, addressed back to the client
A notifications/cancelled message naming every resource the subscription was watching
A result for the original listen request, complete, with the subscription id
Nothing at all, since a notification driven stream never gets a closing message
questions.explanation: A server that ends a subscription on purpose should answer the original listen request with a complete result carrying the subscription id, so the client can tell a clean end from an abrupt transport drop.

questions.question: A stdio server process restarts after a crash. What must the client do to keep receiving the notifications it had subscribed to?
options: Send a Last-Event-ID header so the stream continues from where it left off
Reconnect and wait, since the new process resumes every prior subscription automatically
Do nothing, because subscription state survives a restart on disk
Resend subscriptions/listen with a new id, since the new process remembers nothing
questions.explanation: A restarted server holds no subscription state from before the crash, so the client has to resend subscriptions/listen and rebuild each stream, the same statelessness that governs every other request.
